items.title: Pete Candoli interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, February 15, 1999
items.q: Dizzy was there on the band, Al Killian, me and a good trumpet player, a short guy, Jimmy Pupa from Pittsburgh

ctx.x: Well I was with the band — Teddy Powell had a band. And it was very similar as the First Herd in style. On that band was Buddy DeFranco on clarinet, and there was Boots Mussulli, and Charlie Ventura was on the band, and different guys, George Handy was writing charts for the band, and Eddie Finkel, the composer was writing charts. And it was pretty outside in a sense. And I joined the band. I remember being with the band about three or four months, and I got a call from two attorneys by the name of Vellum and…

rehearsing at Nola Studios in New York. And I don’t quite remember how I got there on a day off or something, but Ray McKinley or someone knew that I was interested and they said well we’re rehearsing at Nola’s and, when you can. So I went there and I sat in and they says, “The job is yours.” I think I was making about seventy dollars for the week with Sonny Dunham at the caverns or something. And it was a good band Sonny Dunham had, really, Uan Rasey was playing lead then, and he was just a kid himself. So I…
Yeah. Quite a trumpet section in 1946. You had Conrad—
